body.x: CES 2025, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, concluded on January 10 in Las Vegas, USA. The Seoul Pavilion, organized at a record scale, achieved meaningful global results.

The Seoul Pavilion, which spanned 1,040 square meters at Eureka Park, CES’s startup-exclusive exhibition hall, represented 16 institutions leading Seoul’s startup ecosystem. The pavilion, supported by three districts (Gangnam, Gwanak, and Geumcheon), five startup support organizations, and eight universities, hosted 104 participating companies and 103 student supporters under the "Team Seoul."
Interview with Yoo Kwangho | Produced by AVING News
Dongguk University Startup Institute (Director Yoo Kwangho) represented major universities in Seoul at CES 2025, highlighting the potential of its local startups in AI and healthcare.

Established in 1999 as a startup incubator certified by South Korea’s Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the institute provides a full-cycle support process, from education to commercialization and incubation, through its four centers. It also plays a pivotal role in fostering a shared, cooperative startup ecosystem with local communities.

At CES 2025, Dongguk University showcased startups such as Mobility One, ENTERTAKE, Medicaretec, SIMSTech, and Reversemountain Corp, aiming to introduce these innovative companies to the global stage.

body.cap: Yoo Kwangho, Director of Dongguk University Startup Institute, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: How do you feel about participating in CES 2025 with startups from Dongguk University?

Yoo Kwangho: Dongguk University Startup Institute supports about 70 new startups annually and incubates over 150 companies. Our goal is to provide continuous support for their growth and expansion. CES, as a global exhibition, aligns perfectly with our mission, offering an opportunity to help local startups step into international markets.
We also aim to gather insights into the latest industry trends, which will serve as a benchmark for shaping our startups’ future strategies.
Q: How were the five participating companies selected?

Yoo Kwangho: CES provides unparalleled opportunities for early-stage startups to explore international markets. The rigorous selection process focused on innovation and growth potential to ensure we bring the most competitive companies to this global platform.

body.cap: Yoo Kwangho, Director of Dongguk University Startup Institute, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: Which participating startups stand out the most?

Yoo Kwangho: Mobility One stands out with its software platform for controlling various unmanned vehicles, from drones to ground robots. With the rising emphasis on automation and advanced mobility, the solution has attracted significant interest from international investors at CES.
Q: What strategies does Dongguk University employ to support global expansion for startups?

Yoo Kwangho: A robust network is crucial for entering foreign markets. We match startups with international partners and encourage participation in initiatives like TIPS to enhance their chances of success.

body.cap: Yoo Kwangho, Director of Dongguk University Startup Institute, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q: What was the reaction from CES visitors to the startups?

Yoo Kwangho: The reception exceeded expectations. For example, ENTERTAKE showcased innovative beauty and healthcare solutions, attracting interest from U.S. and Asian companies. Medicaretec impressed visitors with its device for treating male incontinence, while SIMSTech gained attention for its groundbreaking surgical instrument tracking system.
Q: What are Dongguk University’s goals for 2025?

Yoo Kwangho: Our primary goal is to establish in-house funds to expand investments in local startups. By leveraging university-owned patents and resources, we aim to create an environment where startups can confidently pursue global markets. Successfully launching this initiative at CES 2025 marks an exciting start to this journey.

body.cap: Yoo Kwangho, Director of Dongguk University Startup Institute, interviews with AVING News at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
